walkthroughs.body_html:
A nuclide symbol has the mass number on top and the atomic number below.

For example, chlorine-35 has mass number 35 and atomic number 17. So neutrons = 35 - 17 = 18.

Always do top minus bottom to get neutrons.

Fill shells from the inside out: 2, then 8, then 8.

Argon has 18 electrons, so its configuration is 2,8,8. Potassium has 19, so it goes 2,8,8,1 — the 19th electron starts a new shell.

The group number equals the number of outer-shell electrons. Sodium is 2,8,1 so it's in group 1.

The period number equals the number of shells used. Sodium uses 3 shells so it's in period 3.

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.
In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
